transcript:
Meeting header:
Date: 2026-07-04
Start: 15:00 PDT
Duration: ~64 minutes
Attendees: Maya (Redwood AE), Liam (Redwood SE), Jamal (Oceanline CTO), Rosa (Eng Mgr), Priya (Security), Ethan (DevOps)

Summary:
Quick QBR-style check-in focused on capacity prioritization for an upcoming pilot, security gating (KMS, audit logs), and a plan to accelerate a short performance pilot next week. Decision: pilot scope agreed, Redwood to provide sizing + pricing and schedule benchmark window.

Topics covered:
- Current usage patterns and upcoming spike windows
- Dedicated vs hosted capacity tradeoffs and autoscale knobs
- Security/compliance checklist: KMS, SSO, audit logs, retention
- Pilot scope, success criteria, timeline and owners

Transcript:
[00:00:04] Maya: hey everyone thanks for taking time, we'll do a quick run through capacity and security so we can get the pilot kicked off, um, started next week.
[00:00:18] Jamal: yeah thanks Maya, I'll be brief, traffic's been climbing, we've got a feature launch end of month so the spike windows are daily between 08:00 and 10:00 PT and then a weekend batch on Sundays, those are the main concerns.
[00:00:33] Rosa: and just to add, p95 latency target for our customer flows needs to stay under 350ms otherwise the UX team flags it as unacceptable.
[00:00:45] Liam: ok that's super helpful, so two things we'll scope: an initial pilot on Redwood Hosted to validate latency and cost, and a follow-up plan for Redwood Dedicated if economics make sense. quick question - are you expecting KV cache warmup to be an issue with those peak windows?
[00:01:05] Ethan: yeah on warmup the weekend batch is worst, cold start means a lot more token cost, we've also got some long context prompts for the batch jobs.
[00:01:17] Priya: just to flag security, we need K M S integration for key management, also need audit logs retained for at least 12 months and SSO w/ SAML. SOC2 is a must.
[00:01:31] Maya: great, we can do KMS and we have SOC2 reports, i'll send the redwood security pack after this call. quick clarifying Q - is the preference to keep everything in the cloud region us-west-2 or do you need on-prem/air-gapped for the pilot?
[00:01:50] Jamal: for pilot it's ok to use us-west-2, but long-term we might need a private deployment for certain PII workflows.
[00:02:02] Liam: noted. on capacity, a common pattern is to start with hosted with reserved burst capacity and a short dedicated evaluation - that gives you headroom for the launch without committing to an annual reserved pool. we can tweak autoscale policies to prioritize latency for the 08:00–10:00 windows.
[00:02:21] Rosa: can you explain what 'reserved burst' looks like in practice? do we get guaranteed GPUs during the spike?
[00:02:33] Maya: reserved burst is basically a small committed unit you pay for, plus the option to burst into on-demand capacity up to a max. guarantees are SLA-backed within the committed portion; bursts are best-effort but we prioritize customers with committed capacity.
[00:02:53] Jamal: and what's the failover story if we lose capacity regionally? do you do cross-region fallback?
[00:03:03] Liam: yes, smart routing lets us fallback to a warm model in another region — you can pin model versions and we can set automatic fallback to a smaller-quantized variant to keep traffic flowing while degrading gracefully. there's a perf delta but it's transparent from an API perspective.
[00:03:22] Priya: when you say 'quantized variant' is that acceptable for regulatory workloads? we can't leak data between model variants or regions.
[00:03:33] Maya: good point. we can enforce data residency policies and limit fallback to regions within the permitted set. we'll document that and mark the pilot as 'no cross-border fallback' unless approved.
[00:03:50] Ethan: practical question on metrics — can you provide per-route token cost and tracer maps so our finance/infra folks can build forecasts?
[00:04:01] Liam: yes, Redwood Console exposes token-level cost and latency breakdowns per route. we'll include a sample export for your token mixes.
[00:04:13] Rosa: perfect. also, for the pilot we want to run a 90-minute stress window with our production-like traffic shape — can Redwood run that and capture p50/p95/p99 and token billing deltas?
[00:04:26] Liam: absolutely. we'll schedule a 90m perf window, we'll capture latency percentiles, CPU/GPU utilization, and token cost deltas with kv cache hits/misses.
[00:04:39] Jamal: timeline — we need results before our sprint review on Friday so we can decide whether to commit to dedicated capacity. is that feasible?
[00:04:48] Maya: yes, if we run the pilot early next week we can turn around results within 48 hours. action: redwood to send sizing + pricing today, schedule perf window for Thursday or Friday.
[00:05:01] Priya: security checklist — S S O, RBAC, audit logs, K M S, encryption at rest in transit, and a list of subprocessor vendors. can you confirm subt processors?
[00:05:15] Maya: we'll include the subprocessors in the security pack. for K M S we support customer-managed keys via major cloud KMS providers, and we have H S M integrations for private deployments.
[00:05:29] Ethan: on integration, we use Kubernetes in EKS and have an internal ingress pattern; how does Redwood integrate with our existing routing?
[00:05:40] Liam: if you go hosted you hit our API endpoints, typically fronted by your services. for Dedicated or Private we can set up a V P C peering or private link and run inside your network. we'll share an architecture reference doc.
[00:05:55] Rosa: cost question — do you have bumped pricing for guaranteed low latency, like per-request premium?
[00:06:04] Maya: yes we expose cost levers — dedicated reserved capacity is priced monthly, and you can apply latency-priority tiers which add a premium; we'll model both in the pilot pricing.
[00:06:15] Jamal: i know a competitor gave us a quote that was lower but with very limited observability; our finance loves the lower number but the product team insists on observability + SLOs.
[00:06:26] Maya: fair, we differentiate on observability — per-token and per-route tracing, error analysis. will include tradeoff table in the pricing doc.
[00:06:37] [00:06:40] Speaker 1: um yeah excuse me, quick interjection — do we need to worry about prompt de-duplication or caching between tenants?
[00:06:50] Liam: good q — we have prefix caching and KV cache per customer; we do not share KV cache between customers. there can be reuse within a customer's routes if you enable prefix caching.
[00:07:04] Rosa: for the pilot can we enable aggressive caching to reduce token costs and see the delta?
[00:07:12] Liam: yes, we'll run two passes: one with conservative caching and one aggressive to show cost/latency tradeoffs.
[00:07:21] Priya: encryption — at-rest keys managed by customer's K M S acceptable?
[00:07:27] Maya: yes, customer-managed KMS keys are supported for both hosted (where the keys live in your cloud account) and private deployments.
[00:07:35] Jamal: ok next, let's agree on success criteria for the pilot: p95 < 350ms for main route, end-to-end error rate < 0.5%, and cost per API call within 20% of the estimate.
[00:07:47] Maya: sounds good. we'll put those in the pilot charter and return with a clear pass/fail rubric.
[00:07:55] Ethan: small ops ask — if you do dedicated, how do rollouts work? can we do canary model rollouts and auto-fallback?
[00:08:05] Liam: yes, rollouts support canary and A/B, plus automatic fallback policies. you can pin older model versions while validation runs.
[00:08:15] Rosa: about telemetry retention — question from compliance: how long are traces and logs retained in hosted by default?
[00:08:24] Maya: default 90 days for traces, logs can be extended as an enterprise add-on; we'll include options and costs.
[00:08:34] Priya: we'll need 12 months for audit logs specifically.
[00:08:38] Maya: acknowledged. add to action items.
[00:08:42] [00:09:05] Jamal: ok, can we talk about model variants — we have a use case that needs higher quality for certain flows. what's the recommendation — bigger model, or ensemble / reranking?
[00:09:17] Liam: recommend a hybrid — use a medium model for cheap general flows and route critical queries to a higher-capacity variant or reranker. Redwood Optimize can suggest quantization profiles and cost tradeoffs per workload.
[00:09:33] Rosa: will Optimize run automatically or do we need to run a manual analysis?
[00:09:38] Maya: Optimize gives recommendations; we can run a tailored analysis as part of the pilot and include the quantization suggestion.
[00:09:47] Jamal: anything else on security?
[00:09:50] Priya: one more item — pen test and vulnerability scan reports for the runtime, and a short architecture diagram showing where data is decrypted.
[00:09:58] Liam: we have pen test summaries we can share, and our architecture doc will show key boundaries; we'll redact anything sensitive.
[00:10:10] [00:10:30] Rosa: ok logistics — who owns scheduling the perf window?
[00:10:34] Maya: Redwood will propose two slots, you pick — Liam will run the window with Ethan and provide the telemetry export.
[00:10:44] Ethan: prefer Thursday morning slot.
[00:10:47] Liam: Thursday 09:00 PT works for me.
[00:10:50] Maya: action: Liam to schedule and invite; Maya to send sizing spreadsheet today.
[00:10:57] Jamal: on pricing, what's the expected delta between hosted+burst vs dedicated monthly? give rough percentage so finance knows what to expect.
[00:11:06] Maya: rough rule of thumb — hosted with bursts is 10–20% more per-token at high QPS because of burst premium, dedicated committed pools can be 30–50% cheaper per-token at scale but require a monthly commit. we'll put exact numbers in the sheet.
[00:11:22] [00:11:40] Priya: compliance question — do you support customer-managed logs export to our SIEM?
[00:11:46] Liam: yes, we support log exports via secure delivery (S3, GCS) and can integrate with Splunk/Datadog; we'll provide example pipelines.
[00:11:58] Rosa: test case — can we simulate a surge with concurrent long-context requests to see memory/KV pressure?
[00:12:06] Liam: yes, we'll run a custom traffic shape. please provide a sample corpus and we'll mirror it.
[00:12:15] Ethan: i'll send a sanitized sample.
[00:12:19] Maya: perfect.
[00:12:22] [00:12:50] Jamal: quick commercial note — can you do a time-limited pilot discount if we sign for dedicated within 30 days?
[00:12:58] Maya: we can offer a pilot credit and provisional discount if you commit within the 30-day window after successful pilot. i'll include that in the pricing doc.
[00:13:10] [00:13:30] Rosa: anything we should be aware of with model deprecation? we plan to pin a specific model for the pilot.
[00:13:37] Liam: pinning is supported; deprecation windows are communicated 60 days in advance and we give migration guidance.
[00:13:46] Priya: ok last Q from security — is there a way to do on-prem encryption keys for a hosted trial? we want to ensure our keys never leave our account.
[00:13:58] Maya: yes, customer-managed KMS keeps keys in your cloud account; for absolute key isolation Private deployments are the safer option. we'll outline options.
[00:14:10] [00:14:30] Maya: recap and next steps: Maya send pricing + sizing (TODAY), Liam schedule perf window for Thursday 09:00 PT, Ethan provide sample corpus and peak QPS numbers by Tuesday, Priya and Maya to exchange SOC2 + KMS integration notes.
[00:14:49] Jamal: agreed. thanks everyone.
[00:14:54] Meeting end.
